title: Big Red Mixer
logline: Andy throws a Cornell mixer nobody wants to attend, Michael asks the office what it loves about him, and Jim sees Pam's art while a sticky-note prank on Dwight spirals into a crime wall.
outline: A: Pam shows Jim her sketchbook; Jim is the only one who looks. They plan a one-Post-it prank on Dwight that escalates into his whole desk covered in Pam's drawings; Pam owns it at the meeting. B: Michael's "Things I Love About Michael" whiteboard gets a dud; Andy's Cornell mixer draws only Michael and Kevin, and Michael hides tears behind a receipt. Dwight vs. Andy: Andy tries too hard and backfires; an armed truce over a mug. C: Angela defends Dwight bizarrely; Oscar and Kevin know. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, B, A, B, A, C, B, tag.
theme: Being seen: people want someone to actually look at them, not just applaud.
storySoFar: Michael still chases Jan's approval; Jan keeps sending maybes and her voicemail said she isn't coming. Jim and Pam keep escalating Jell-O pranks on Dwight; Jim noticed Pam's earrings, and Roy noticed late and got it wrong. Pam is an artist; Jim is the first person to really look at her sketches. Roy keeps postponing the wedding. Angela thanks Dwight publicly for fax checks; Oscar and Kevin know the secret and say nothing. Andy Bernard arrived from Stamford and tries too hard to be liked; Dwight is at war with him, and a fragile truce is forming. Michael keeps setting out a folding chair for Toby, who sat in it once. Gerald Boyd gave Scranton a barely pass and may return. Stanley is at 212 days, counting down each morning.

stateChanges.arc: Will They, Won't They: Jim and Pam
stateChanges.progress: Pam shows Jim her sketchbook and he is the only one who looks; he shares the blame for the Post-it prank and she finds her voice by admitting she did it because nobody looks at what she makes.
The Things I Love About Michael board gets almost nothing; Michael hides tears behind a Big Red receipt at Andy's mixer, with only Kevin noticing.
Andy's mixer and mug backfire; Dwight and Andy reaffirm the split: Dwight keeps the title, Andy keeps the crowd, and they shake on it.
Angela defends Dwight's face and honesty bizarrely in front of Oscar and Kevin; Oscar's look at the camera says everything; nobody says anything.

stateChanges.status: closer; she shows him her art and he is the only one who looks

stateChanges.text: Pam's sticky-note drawings of Dwight are now on the conference room crime wall; Michael said he wants to see the rest of her work.
Andy's Cornell mixer: only Michael and Kevin came. Andy's Big Red receipt ($34) is in Michael's wallet.
Dwight attended the mixer 'in my capacity as Assistant to the Regional Manager.' Andy made him a Cornell mug; Dwight accepted it as a token of surrender.
Kevin: 'Nobody say nothing.' Used in the cold open, the prank, the mixer, and the Angela scene.
Stanley's countdown: 212 at the cold open, 211 in the tag.
Michael's 'Things I Love About Michael' board: one percentage (61%) from Dwight and an M&Ms note from Kevin.

scenes.recap: Andy offers lopsided Cornell cookies to a break room that would rather not.

beats.text: Good morning, Scranton! I baked Cornell cookies. Red and white. Go Big Red!

beats.caption: presents a tray of lopsided cookies like a championship trophy
The microwave beeps. Nobody moves.

beats.text: Those are not cookies, Andy. Those are a hostage situation.
It's my grandmother's recipe!

lines: Andy wants everybody to like him. Two hundred and twelve days left for me. I'm not making it easier.

beats.caption: takes five cookies and eats them in four slow bites

beats.text: Good cookie. Thank you.
Thank you, Kevin! Have another!
Nobody say nothing.

scenes.recap: Pam hesitantly shows Jim her sketchbook, and he is the only one who really looks.

beats.text: Don't look at this. It's really bad.
Okay.

beats.caption: looks at the sketchbook for a long time, very carefully

beats.text: This is the copier. It looks like it's about to sigh.
It does sigh. Every time.

beats.caption: Jim keeps turning the page.

beats.text: You drew the water cooler. Nobody draws the water cooler.
It's where everybody stands. It's the middle of the office.
The reflection in it is really good, Pam.

lines: Roy looked at my sketchbook for four seconds. He asked if the copier was supposed to be a dog.
It was a copier, Roy. Jim just knew it was a copier.

beats.text: Keep drawing, okay?

scenes.recap: Michael asks the office to write one thing they love about him, and the board gets almost nothing.

beats.text: This is a no-judgment zone. I want one thing you love about me. Anything.

beats.caption: writes THINGS I LOVE ABOUT MICHAEL across the whiteboard in fat letters
The marker squeaks.

beats.text: Your bold Scranton spirit! Your leadership! I love all of you, Michael. The whole you.
Andy, that's a lot. That's a lot of me.

beats.caption: writes a percentage in tiny, precise block capitals

beats.text: What's sixty-one percent?
Sixty-one percent of this office loves you. It is a fact.
Who's the other thirty-nine?
Question: Do you want me to go through them?
No. No, I'm good.
Michael. Also M&Ms.
Toby, you're not invited to this.
I'm in the room, Michael.

lines: He asks for feedback, then uninvites me from the feedback.
I've stopped taking it personally. Mostly.

beats.text: Can we go? I'm counting.

beats.caption: One percentage, one M&Ms, and a whole lot of white board.

beats.text: Great. Honest feedback. Meeting adjourned. I'm a rock.

scenes.recap: Angela thanks Dwight in front of Oscar and Kevin and defends him in a way that makes no sense.

beats.text: Dwight checked the fax again today. He is a very thorough man.
Actually, checking the fax is his job, Angela.
He did it well. Kevin, don't you agree?
Nobody say nothing.
Question: Who is talking about me?
Dwight, thank you for checking the fax. Publicly.
It was jammed with cat hair. It is an honor to be thanked by a Party Planner.
Dwight would never draw on anything. He respects paper far too much. He is the most honest man in this building.

lines: Angela has said Dwight's name six times in one minute. I'm an accountant. I counted.
Nobody is saying anything. That is the entire problem.

beats.text: Dwight has a Jell-O trophy, Angela.
Nobody say nothing.

scenes.recap: Jim and Pam plan a single tiny Post-it prank on Dwight, which Jim already knows is not going to stay tiny.

beats.text: Dwight's desk is sacred. We don't touch it.
We don't have to touch it. We could just leave one thing on it.
What thing?
A drawing. Of him. On a Post-it. It's very small.
Pam. That's the best idea we've had.
Just one. On his monitor. He won't even notice.
Dwight notice everything. Dwight is police.

lines: Pam draws like she's apologizing to the thing she's drawing.
I'm not saying I'm in love. I'm saying I'm holding the Post-its.

beats.caption: Kevin nods very slowly.

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.

scenes.recap: Andy announces a Cornell mixer that nobody asked for, and Dwight treats it as a hostile takeover.

beats.text: Cornell alumni mixer! Today! Lunch! Annex! Bring your Big Red!
Question: Is this a mixer or a takeover?
It's a mixer, Dwight. For community.
Oh my god, is there a DJ?
I'm a DJ. Kind of. I have a banjo.
Will there be pretzels?
There will be pretzels.
Then I'm not going. I'm saving myself for Pretzel Day.

beats.caption: sings a verse of the Cornell fight song to the flyer
The flyer curls at one corner.

beats.text: False. You are trying to replace Michael's Friday lunch with a sing-along.
Maybe you could come? As, like, the ambassador?
Question: Is that a bribe? I will attend in my capacity as Assistant to the Regional Manager.

scenes.recap: Jim and Pam's one-Post-it prank turns into Dwight's whole desk covered in Pam's drawings.

beats.caption: sticks a blank Post-it on the bottom of Dwight's monitor

beats.text: Just one.

beats.caption: draws a tiny Dwight face on a second Post-it, very carefully

beats.text: That's him. That's exactly him.

beats.caption: adds a third Post-it, then a fourth, then one on the stapler

beats.text: Okay, now the stapler is in Jell-O.
Jim, no—

beats.caption: sets the stapler in lime Jell-O, then tapes drawings to the chair

beats.text: False. Someone has been in my desk.
Dwight, why is your desk wearing your face?
It is an attack. Question: Will you help me investigate?
Who would attack you?

beats.caption: slides a Post-it into his shirt pocket, face calm

scenes.recap: Andy's mixer draws Michael and Kevin, and Michael hides a tear behind a Big Red receipt.

beats.text: Michael! You came! Three people! That's a mixer by Cornell math.
I'm not Cornell, Andy. I'm Scranton. But I like you.

beats.caption: sings the Cornell alma mater with one hand on his heart

beats.text: Is this a mixer or a hostage situation?

beats.caption: pulls a Big Red receipt for thirty-four dollars from his wallet

beats.text: Thirty-four dollars of soda. For a crowd of three.

beats.caption: hides a tear behind the receipt

lines: It's not crying. It's Big Red. It's a very strong drink.
I'm a rock. I'm a rock with a receipt.

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.

beats.caption: Andy beams. Stanley leaves.

beats.text: Best mixer I've ever been to. Honestly.

scenes.recap: At an emergency meeting, Pam admits to the drawings, and Jim admits he helped, and Michael asks to see more of her work.

beats.text: Someone has been drawing on Dwight. This is now a crime room.

beats.caption: pins Pam's Post-its across the whiteboard like evidence

beats.text: Question: Is this about the Jell-O?
Actually, these are good. Someone drew the eyes.
The eyes are not me. I do not have that expression.
Who did this?

beats.caption: Pam raises her hand, then lowers it.

beats.text: I did. Dwight, I'm sorry. I did it.
I stuck them up. That's basically drawing.
Question: Why?
Because nobody here looks at anything I make.

beats.caption: Jim is looking at her. Nobody else is.

beats.text: Pam, I'd like to see the rest. Show me the rest.
Okay.

scenes.recap: Angela defends Dwight's face as though it were a national treasure, and nobody follows up.

beats.text: Whoever did this is a monster. Dwight's face is precious.
Angela, it's a face on a Post-it.
It's his face. Dwight deserves someone who respects his face.
Nobody say nothing.
Thank you, Angela.
I'm not thanking you. I'm thanking the fax.

beats.caption: Oscar looks at the ceiling. Kevin opens a bag of M&Ms.

beats.text: Noted.

scenes.recap: Andy gives Dwight a Cornell mug and tries too hard, and the two shake on an armed truce.

beats.text: Dwight. I got you a Cornell mug. I'm trying here.
Question: Is this a bribe?
No! Also, I put your name on the mixer gift card.
It says Dwight Schrute, Assistant to the Regional Manager. That is a conspiracy.
I wanted you to feel valued!

beats.caption: Andy's hand is still out, holding the mug.

beats.text: You keep the crowd. I keep the title.
Deal. Can we shake on it?

beats.caption: shakes Andy's hand once, firmly, like a hostage exchange

beats.text: Okay. I'm also working on my anger.
Noted.

scenes.recap: In the parking lot, Pam says Roy missed the earrings again, and Jim says they're the good ones.

beats.text: Roy didn't notice my earrings again.
They're the good ones.

beats.caption: Pam touches one earring and smiles.

lines: Roy didn't notice the earrings again.
I noticed. I'm not saying that's a big deal. It's a big deal.

beats.text: Two hundred and eleven. Don't talk to me.
